issues.description: The solution implementation references the global symbol 'display_start' but does not declare it. The problem statement and the template declare 'display_start' (frame buffer base) in .bss, while the solution removed or relocated that declaration but still uses the identifier (e.g. add eax, display_start and mov esi, display_start). This will cause assembly/link errors or undefined behavior and conflicts with the expectation in the problem statement that a memory label display_start exists.
issues.suggestedFix: Restore a proper declaration of the frame-buffer base symbol in the solution (e.g. add 'section .bss' and 'display_start RESB 8294400' as in the template) or explicitly allocate/initialize and reference an equivalent symbol. Ensure the symbol is declared before any references (or adjust code to use a passed-in address) so the assembly and intended behavior match the problem specification.
